A configuration to compare in a benchmark

Source: R/core-bench-arm.R
hr_arm.Rd

An arm is one way of answering the items of a reference: a prompt, a model, a reading recipe, a baseline that calls no model at all. It is a function run(item, ctx) that returns the arm's output for one item, which the benchmark's scorer then compares with the item's label.

Usage

hr_arm(name, run, params = list(), derived_from = NULL, version = "0.0.1")

Arguments

name

The arm's name: one non-blank string, unique within a benchmark.

run

A function of (item, ctx) returning the arm's output for one item: what the scorer is given (see hr_scorer()). item is the item's payload from hr_reference().

params

A named list of the settings that make this arm what it is. They are recorded with the benchmark and reach run as ctx$params.

derived_from

The name of the arm this one is built from (for an arm that reuses another's draws offline), or NULL.

version

The arm's version, one string. Change it when the arm's behaviour changes, so results from before and after can be told apart.

Value

An object of class hr_arm: a list of name, run, params, derived_from, version and hash, a SHA-256 hash of the other five that changes when the arm's code, settings or version do. The code is hashed as text, with the values it names from the environment it was made in: the workspace for an arm written at top level, or the function of yours that built it. So an arm that reads a global prompt has a new hash when that prompt changes, and the same arm has the same hash in every session and after saveRDS(). A function from a package is hashed by its code and the package's name.

Details

ctx is a list with

client

The client given to hr_benchmark().

trace

A gr_trace() of this run alone. Every request the arm makes must be recorded into it (gr_call(..., trace = ctx$trace)): it is how the benchmark counts the run's tokens, dollars and refusals, and how it holds the run to the benchmark's limits.

governor

The hr_governor() the run is held to: the benchmark's limits less what earlier runs used. It is already attached to trace.

draw_index

The run number, 1 to runs. Pass it to gr_call() as draw_index so each run is its own draw: under a gr_cache() or a gr_replay_client() a request sent without it answers every run with the same stored reply, and the benchmark refuses such an arm.

call

A shortcut, ctx$call(messages, ...), for gr_call(ctx$client, messages, ..., trace = ctx$trace, draw_index = ctx$draw_index).

item_id, arm, run, params

The item's id, the arm's name, the run number and the arm's params.

See also

hr_benchmark(), hr_reference(), hr_scorer()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

short <- hr_arm("short", function(item, ctx) {
  ctx$call(paste("Answer in one word:", item))$text
}, params = list(prompt = "one word"))
short
#> <hr_arm short> version 0.0.1
#>   params: prompt = one word 
#>   hash: 8c436eb80f4b
